title: Reduce embedding endpoint tail latency via microbatch rebalancing and kernel telemetry
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Objective: Reduce 99th-percentile latency for the embeddings endpoint by addressing microbatch variance, improving kernel selection signals, and adding targeted telemetry to identify stragglers. Background: Customers running large-scale reranking and semantic search report intermittent p99 spikes (current median p99 ~ 230ms on vector endpoints under 70% load). Hypothesis: a combination of microbatch skew (small high-priority requests not coalescing), suboptimal kernel routing for short-context embedding models, and lack of early warning telemetry are the primary contributors. This ticket consolidates a set of experiments, telemetry and short-term mitigations to stabilize tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce embedding endpoint p99 by at least 30% under representative load (measured on perf harness for model redwood/emb-small-v2)
No more than 5% regression in median latency after changes
Introduce kernel selection telemetry that attributes per-request kernel choice and kernel exec time for at least 90% of requests
Documented rollout plan with canary success criteria and dashboard links
plan: Phase A: Add lightweight kernel telemetry and microbatch histogram tracing (instrument ingress and runtime path)
Phase B: Implement microbatch rebalance policy (timebox-based aggressive coalescing for short requests + backoff for heavy requests)
Phase C: Kernel affinity labels and small-context fastpath tuning (change kernel hints for <=64 token embeddings)
Phase D: Canary rollout with 5% traffic, monitor p50/p95/p99 and request-drop metrics, then ramp to 25%/100%
Phase E: Postmortem and make config defaults if successful
experiments: Experiment 1: Microbatch timebox reduction from 8ms -> 4ms for tenant classes with low throughput (expected to reduce small request latency at cost of some batching efficiency)
Experiment 2: Opportunistic coalescing flag that prefers packing short requests together using a 'size-first' queue; evaluate throughput vs tail latency
Experiment 3: Kernel hint prioritization for <=64-token requests to route to fastpath kernels (A/B test against current selector)
Experiment 4: Per-request speculative prefetch of KV cache for predictable tenants to avoid cold-kv stalls
Experiment 5: Quantized-kernel fallback when kernel exec time exceeds threshold (safety to avoid single-request long-tail spends)
Experiment 6: Synthetic straggler injection test to validate detection and preemptive re-routing
metrics: Operational: kernel_exec_time_ms per kernel type, microbatch_size_distribution histogram, queue_wait_ms, admission_reject_rate
risks: Aggressive microbatch reduction could increase per-token cost due to smaller effective batch sizes
Kernel affinity changes may expose regressions for certain quantized models; need rollback plan
Telemetry overhead could slightly increase median latency if not sampled carefully
Incorrect tenant classification may cause unfair latencies across customers
comments: 2026-02-16 Sofia Patel: Initial triage complete. Reproduced p99 spikes on perf harness with the reranking workload. Baseline recorded: median p99=232ms, p95=78ms, median=42ms.

2026-02-20 Marco Liu: Added kernel telemetry prototype to runtime branch. Telemetry emits kernel_name and exec_ms per request to event stream (sampling 20%). Observed that ~12% of p99 requests used fallback kernel with 3x exec time.

2026-02-27 Anika Romero (SRE): Run synthetic straggler injection. Found that when single request locks GPU due to fragmentation, backpressure delays following requests by up to 160ms. Suggest adding preemptive queue admission limit per-stream.

2026-03-03 Marco Liu: Deployed microbatch timebox experiment on canary (5% traffic). Early results: p99 on canary down 18% but throughput efficiency reduced by ~6%. Collecting more data before wider rollout.

2026-03-08 Product review (Evan Cho): Acceptable tradeoff if p99 reduction exceeds 25% and cost increase <10% for affected tenants. Approved continued experiments and to prepare customer communication template.
2026-03-10 Sofia Patel: Merging kernel affinity tuning PR after tests. Next step: implement canary monitoring alerts and schedule 25% ramp on 2026-03-12 if no regressions.
